fatal_errors: The hypothesis assigns embrittlement to grain-boundary segregation, whereas the target mechanism is intraphase L12 ordering coupled to jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries without intergranular impurity segregation.
It incorrectly treats the starting material as single-phase; the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy is initially FCC plus B2.
It omits the intermediate-temperature aging window and the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition, including minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
explanation: The response addresses HEA toughness degradation only at a broad level and predicts generic embrittlement. It does not reconstruct the thermal-aging intervention, relevant 550–750°C window, L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, jagged phase-boundary stress concentrations, or ductile transition zones. Its proposed comparison is weakly discriminating because 'controlled introduction' of segregation and nanoclustering is undefined and could alter many variables. A decisive target-aligned test would correlate ordering and phase-boundary morphology with dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation across aging temperatures while excluding grain-boundary impurity segregation.
